                                             I. INTRODUCTION

Robert Lee Noland, P.E. Retired, pro se Intervener timely file this Initial Post-Hearing
Brief opposing Segments F34, G43, G44 and G45, under SOAH Order No. 6.


                                    II. SUMMARY OF ARGUMENT

After 5 days of hearing, there was not a single expert, party or landowner that
advocated for any routes utilizing Segments F34, G43, G44, or G45 nor were those
segments even mentioned in any cross-examination. They weren't included in any of the
focus routes. Furthermore, these 4 segments were included in only 17 of the 122 routes
(only 13.93%) that were selected and submitted by Casey Petty, PE, PMP to be filed with
the CCN Application1. The reason is clear. Routes including these segments
underperform in most of the PURA factor categories listed on the Environmental
Assessment2. At a minimum, they are more expensive, longer, affect more habitable
structures, cross more than double the amount of cultural resources sites, and come
within 1,000 feet of cultural resource sites more than three times than that of Route 894.3
Staying within at least 500 feet of the centerline, Segment G44 parallels the Russell Fork
of the San Gabriel River ("San Gabriel") its entire length and crosses the San Gabriel
numerous times, impetuously fracturing tracts of generational land. Deciding on a route
that includes Segments F34, G43, G44, or G45 makes zero sense and would go against
what is required under PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B). Making the
decision on what route to choose isn't the hard part, it is living with that choice.

The Applicants overlooked and therefore made no effort to offset the Transmission Line
to avoid the Florence Elementary School and the future highway interchange on Link
F34. It follows that Link F34 should be removed from consideration for any Route.

The ALJs, PUCT and ERCOT needs to do the right thing for Texas Grid Reliability:
   1. Texas needs Generation to provide power for winter storms, hot summers and
      large loads
   2. Should transmission lines be needed that comes second after generation




1
    Oncor & LCRATSC, Exh. 1 at 1988-1991.

59475 - Party 245 - Robert Lee Noland - Initial Brief                              Page 3 of 10
                                               III. ARGUMENT

I oppose all routes that include Segments F34, G43, G44, or G45 because of the
significant negative environmental impact and harm to community values in the area,
including the cost, habitable structure count, and the effect on generational land. The
ALJs and Commission should select a route that avoids the southernmost portion of the
study area and the San Gabriel to avoid these concerns that should be fatal to selection
of any route through that area.

                      Florence Elementary School and Highway Interchange

The Applicants overlooked the Florence Elementary School and the future highway
interchange on Link F34. Applicants did not make an effort to avoid the school or the
highway interchange since they were not aware of either of them.

        The Florence ISD Superintendent in his direct testimony describes the location
         and the description of the school.4

        Avoid Schools

                 Russell Marusak testified schools should be avoided and that he was not
                 aware of the school when the links and routes were identified for this
                 project.5

        Many Buildable Alternatives

                 Russell Marusak testified that there are many other acceptable and
                 buildable routes most of which do not use Link F34.

        Avoid People

                 Russell Marusak emphasized when making routing decisions they tried to
                 avoid habitable structures since structures contain people. It follows that
                 the Florence Elementary school contains hundreds of people during the
                 school day and thus should also be avoided.


4
    Egnyte: 226- Florence Independent School District - Admitted Exhibits
Florence ISD - Exhibit 1 - Witness Testimony - FISD 005
Rick Kirkpatrick, Superintendent of Florence Independent School District
5
    Interchange 6137 - SOAH Docket 473-26-16349 HOM V3 Marusak Cross Pages 42-54


59475 - Party 245 - Robert Lee Noland - Initial Brief                               Page 4 of 10
        Our children are our future

                 It should go without saying that we should do what we can to protect our
                 children since they are our future. Their future rests on several
                 interconnected logical, moral, and practical arguments derived from
                 societal continuity and intergenerational responsibility.



                 The phrase 'Moral Obligation and Stewardship' invokes a moral duty to
                 provide a livable, fair, and equitable world for children. Adults hold
                 temporary positions of power and responsibility, with the understanding
                 that they will eventually hand these duties over. Therefore, there is our
                 collective obligation to provide early childhood health and education.



       We should learn from the past.

                 Scientists cannot prove with absolute certainty that exposure to a 765kV
                 500Amp extra high voltage power lines will not cause negative effects, so
                 lets look at the past items that were considered normal in my childhood
                 and were deemed to be ‘just fine’ till we took the time to learn about
                 them, then they were not.



                 I am 84 years old. When I went to elementary school, lead was used in
                 paint and gasoline and that was normal. Folks just did not understand
                 Lead Poisoning back then. Polychlorinated biphenyls or PCBs were
                 normally used in the capacitors and transformers used by electrical
                 utilities. I remember handling Mercury and placing it on Dime or Quarter
                 in Junior high science class. I also remember folks that allowed their kids
                 run and play behind the trucks that were spraying DDT to kill mosquitos in
                 most every neighborhood in Texas. This is just a few of our failures in a
                 long list, but I feel you get the point.




59475 - Party 245 - Robert Lee Noland - Initial Brief                                Page 5 of 10
                   During my lifetime we have learned of many devastating toxins to children,
                  caused by a long list of exposures that were assumed safe in my
                  childhood. It just takes time for adults to figure these things out.



        Many professions are important enough to be Licensed by the State of
         Texas.

                  Though I am retired, I still maintain my Professional Engineering license to
                  practice in Texas. It establishes a legal standard of competency to
                  protecting public health, safety and welfare as we design infrastructure for
                  the public. It is important to be ethically bound to consider public safety.



        Costs seem minimal to potentially avoid a hazardous environment

                  It may not yet be clear what the effects will be of living or going to school
                  under a 765kV, 500Amp extra high voltage power line. We can not
                  determine with any amount of certainty that a mother's fetus or small child
                  being exposed to an extra high voltage powerline will not cause negative
                  effects. Given the choice, it should be avoided since we just don't know the
                  long term effects.

        Mr. Poole of PUC Staff explained that from reviewing the application it was
         apparent that the applicants were not aware of either the elementary school or
         the highway interchange on Link F34. Normally a reasonable effort should have
         been expended by the applicants to offset the powerline to avoid the elementary
         school and the highway interchange. Further that the purpose of avoiding
         habitable structures was to avoid exposing humans to the power line and the
         associated electromagnetic radiation. It follows that prudent actions during
         routing should have been taken to avoid exposing a school with 530 students to
         the power line and associated electro magnetic radiation.6




6
    Interchange 6137 Hearing Transcript from Wednesday 6/10/26 - Pages 95 to 102
Cross Examination of Mr. Poole (PUC Staff) by #374 Kevin Kennedy

                           Prudent Avoidance; 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)(iv)

The Commission defines prudent avoidance as "[The limiting of exposures to electric
and magnetic fields that can be avoided with reasonable investments of money and
effort."7 Prudent avoidance also considers what can be done in different settings, such
as rural versus urban areas, where routing options and the opportunities to make
routing changes differ. This does not mean a proposed transmission line must avoid
habitable structures at all costs, but reasonable alternatives must be considered.8
Maximizing distance from residences was the highest priority for respondents to Joint
Applicants' open-house questionnaires.9


                      Texas Needs Generation before Transmission Lines

The ALJs, PUCT and ERCOT needs to do the right thing for Texas Grid Reliability:
    Texas needs Generation to provide power for winter storms, hot summers and
      large loads
    Should transmission lines be needed that comes second after generation

Instead of Texas committing nearly $100 Billion (with a "B") lifetime cost to the rate
payers for transmission lines, Texas should take the time to determine and fund the
necessary power generation capacity to avoid a Texas power outage during a future
winter storm or hot summer.

It is well known that the output of Renewable Energy, specifically solar and wind power,
fluctuates based on weather conditions and time of day. Texas first needs a “Generation
Plan” to provide enough power during times when the sun doesn't shine and the wind
doesn't blow thus avoiding a power outage during a future major winter storm or hot
summer.




7
    16 TAC § 25.101(a)(4).
8
    Application of LCRA Transmission Services Corporation to Amend its Certificate of
Convenience and necessity for the Proposed EC Mornhinweg to Parkway 138 -
kVTransmission Line in Comal and Guadalupe Counties , Docket No . 40684, Order at
FoF 84 (Jun. 19, 2013).
9
    Oncor & LCRA TSC, Exh. 1 at 203


59475 - Party 245 - Robert Lee Noland - Initial Brief                            Page 7 of 10
 This concern is amplified during power disturbances, or spikes of excessive high or low
power that impacts grid stability. Disturbances may be mitigated by having enough
'system inertia' to ride out the disturbance. Intermittency and reduced system inertia,
create challenges in maintaining the real-time balance between electricity supply and
demand.

Traditional thermal power generation (coal, nuclear and natural gas) rely on the physical
momentum of spinning turbines to stabilize the grid frequency against these
disturbances. Renewal energy sources like solar and wind turbines connect to the grid
via electronic inverters that provide little to no inherent inertia. As renewal penetration
increases, the grid becomes more sensitive to imbalances; frequency can deviate rapidly
should a cloud pass over or wind drops, increasing the risk of cascading failures.

To mitigate grid instability, the PUCT and ERCOT should build in grid stability solutions
including thermal generation and batteries.

Failure to do so leads down a slippery slope towards a widespread blackout.

When there is insufficient power on the grid, the frequency drops below 60Hz. The
demand for electrical current exceeds the generation capacity causing generators to
slow down. As they struggle, it leads to brownouts or voltage drops. Load must be
quickly reduced to prevent immediate grid failure.

If the deficit persists or is severe, grid operators should implement rolling blackouts or
load shedding to disconnect non-critical areas, stabilizing the remaining network for
essential services.

Without these interventions, the frequency deviation can cause protective actions that
disconnect generators, triggering a cascading failure and a widespread blackout.

Examples include:
 ▪ The 2021 Texas Power Crisis triggered by severe winter storm Uri.
 ▪ The 2003 major Northeast Blackout that affected 50 million people in both the US and
Canada.

Again, we should plan the generation to support stability and worst case power demand
during tough winter and summer conditions. Once generation and loads are
understood, then plan any needed transmission lines.




59475 - Party 245 - Robert Lee Noland - Initial Brief                             Page 8 of 10
                                              IV. CONCLUSION

         Eliminate or do not use Link F34 to avoid the Florence Elementary School

         Routes including Links G43, G44 and G45 are more expensive, longer, have

          considerably more habitable structures and threaten approximately 20 miles of the San

          Gabriel River along Segment G44

         Provide the necessary generation to stabilize the grid and avoid winter storms

Remembering that the choice of route isn't the hard part, its living with what you choose. Choose

wisely.
